title: Mathematical model for non-monotone dose response to the PD-L1 blockade in vitro
task: Mathematical modeling of non-monotonic dose-response in PD-L1 checkpoint inhibition
key_results: Model estimates Cmax_resp (optimal therapeutic concentration) and EC50 values from luminescence data; discriminates target-specific bioactivity from concentration-dependent toxicity across dose range
comments: The non-monotonic response (biphasic curve) is mechanistically captured, making this valuable for drug optimization, though validation against additional immunotherapy targets would strengthen generalizability.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Non-monotonic dose response arises from concentration-dependent toxicity competing with target-specific T-cell activation
hypotheses.result: Model successfully explains biphasic luminescence curves and enables separation of efficacy from toxicity parameters

task: Automated acute lymphoblastic leukemia diagnosis from blood smears via vision-CNN fusion
key_results: ConfuNetHMA achieved 100% accuracy on ALL dataset, 97.39% on C-NMC; ROC-AUC = 0.994 for ALL subtype differentiation; Grad-CAM + LIME/SHAP/Integrated Gradients provide concordant explainability aligned with hematological criteria
comments: 100% accuracy on one dataset suggests potential overfitting or dataset-specific bias; clinical deployment requires external prospective validation.

model_io.model: ConfuNetHMA (Vision Transformer + CNN with meta-attention fusion)
outputs: Explainability heatmaps (Grad-CAM, LIME, SHAP, Integrated Gradients)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fusion of global (ViT) and local (CNN) feature representations via meta-attention improves ALL diagnostic accuracy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; achieved near-perfect classification on benchmark datasets
